newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.00/05 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.00/05 percent.

text.p: German call money was quoted at unchanged rates of 3.00/05 percent on Friday in a relatively quiet market.
Dealers said some demand had emerged as a result of tax payments draining funds from the market, and there were almost no funds on offer at a three percent rate.

Dealers said reserve levels were comfortable, but that they did not expect additional relief from tax funds flowing back into the market until next week. "The figures are good, but they are not generous," one trader said.
Banks held 38.3 billion marks in reserves on Thursday.
That compared with 38.3 billion marks on Wednesday.
The average for the first 14 days of the month eased to 39.8 billion marks from 39.9 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.05300 on Friday compared with 3.04950 on Wednesday.
